metadata.summary: England Lions thumped their highest List A score of all time as they piled on 487-5 from 50 overs against West Indies A in the second unofficial ODI in St Kitts.
metadata.content: England Lions hit their highest List A cricket score of 487-5 as Durham's Ben McKinney smashes 145 from 65 balls | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content England Lions hit their highest List A cricket score of 487-5 as Durham's Ben McKinney smashes 145 from 65 balls Durham opener Ben McKinney smashes 15 fours and 10 sixes in his eye-catching century as England Lions make it five wins from five on West Indies tour; James Rew also scores a ton as Lions eclipse the Ben Duckett-inspired 425-1 the Lions amassed against Sri Lanka A in Canterbury in 2016 Tuesday 10 November 2026 07:09, UK Image: Durham opener Ben McKinney smashed 15 fours and 10 sixes in his century as England Lions made it five wins from five on their West Indies tour England Lions thumped their highest List A score of all time as they piled on 487-5 from 50 overs against West Indies A in the second unofficial ODI in St Kitts. The total, in which Durham opener Ben McKinney looted 145 from 65 deliveries and James Rew scored 107 not out from 56, eclipsed the 425-1 the side racked up against Sri Lanka A at Canterbury a decade ago. In that match, current England Test and ODI opener Ben Duckett plundered 220 not out from 131 balls and Kent's Daniel Bell-Drummond 171 from 139 after Dawid Malan had fallen for 23. metadata.summary: Aryna Sabalenka got off to a winning start at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells, battling past Karolina Muchova 7-6 (7-2) 7-5, while Mirra Andreeva was also victorious in her Group 2 opener on Monday.
metadata.content: WTA Finals: Aryna Sabalenka battles past Karolina Muchova in her opening match at Indian Wells | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content WTA Finals: Aryna Sabalenka battles past Karolina Muchova in her opening match at Indian Wells Aryna Sabalenka won her Group 2 opener against Karolina Muchova 7-6 (7-2) 7-5, while Mirra Andreeva made light work of Elina Svitolina in a 6-4 6-0 triumph; watch the WTA Finals from Indian Wells this week, live on Sky Sports Tennis Tuesday 10 November 2026 00:02, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Aryna Sabalenka against Karolina Muchova from the WTA Finals. Aryna Sabalenka got off to a winning start at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells, battling past Karolina Muchova 7-6 (7-2) 7-5, while Mirra Andreeva was also victorious in her Group 2 opener on Monday. A two-time beaten finalist in the WTA Finals - including going down last year to Elena Rybakina, who stole her No 1 ranking this season - Sabalenka is looking to win the tournament for the first time. Rybakina's late withdrawal due to a viral illness and fatigue aids Sabalenka's hopes, as does her opening victory over Wimbledon finalist Muchova, who made her sweat for it in a hugely-absorbing contest that ran six minutes shy of two hours. metadata.summary: Josh Allen threw a touchdown pass with 44 seconds left before half-time, James Cook rushed 31 times for 107 yards and a late score, and the Buffalo Bills beat Minnesota 23-6 on Monday night, sending Vikings deeper into their unrelenting offensive slump.
metadata.content: Josh Allen's Buffalo Bills dominate slumping Minnesota Vikings to improve to 7-1 | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Josh Allen's Buffalo Bills dominate slumping Minnesota Vikings to improve to 7-1 The Buffalo Bills improve to 7-1 on the season as they take advantage of a sputtering Minnesota Vikings in a 23-6 win on Monday night; the NFL returns to Europe on Sunday when the Detroit Lions face the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany, live on Sky Sports NFL from 2pm Tuesday 10 November 2026 07:16, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Buffalo Bills against the Minnesota Vikings from Week 9 of the NFL season. Josh Allen threw a touchdown pass with 44 seconds left before half-time, James Cook rushed 31 times for 107 yards and a late score, and the Buffalo Bills beat Minnesota 23-6 on Monday night, sending Vikings deeper into their unrelenting offensive slump. Linebackers Terrel Bernard and Dorian Williams had interceptions and Tyler Bass made four field goals to stretch his franchise-record streak to 25 straight as the Bills (7-1) matched their best eight-game start since 1993. That season ended with their last of four straight Super Bowl losses. With Kyler Murray sidelined by a hamstring injury, Carson Wentz started at quarterback for the Vikings (6-2) and didn't finish what became one of the worst performances of his 11-year career.
